hero.oneLiner: One of India's leading circular-economy players, recovering and recycling end-of-life energy storage products and non-ferrous scrap into pure lead and lead alloys of 99.97%-99.985% purity.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's leading circular-economy players, recovering and recycling end-of-life energy storage products and non-ferrous scrap into pure lead and lead alloys of 99.97%-99.985% purity.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Ardee Industries Limited recycles used lead-acid batteries and other recyclable scrap (battery scrap, remelted lead ingots and blocks, lead scrap from radio/relay/ropes, lead master metal) into pure lead and customisable lead alloys - lead calcium, lead antimony, lead tin, lead silver and lead cadmium - at a single 7.61-acre facility in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh with 104,025 MTPA installed capacity. Output is sold to lead-acid battery manufacturers and metal customers, with Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited as a key customer, and to exporters across seven countries. As of March 31, 2025 the company had served more than 50 customers, selling in ten Indian states and exporting to Singapore, Hong Kong, South Korea, Switzerland, UAE, Japan and the USA.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Pure Lead:** Pure lead ingots, purity 99.97% to 99.985%, conforming to international standards, Brand 'Ardee' listed on the MCX platform for trading in pure lead

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Closed-loop / backward-integrated circular model: the Company runs in-house procurement of waste material, sorting, recycling and production, converting end-of-life energy storage products (used lead-acid batteries) and non-ferrous scrap into pure lead and lead alloy ingots at a single owned Manufacturing Facility in District Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh (7.61 acres, 104,025 MTPA installed). Backward linkage is through a global sourcing network — raw materials imported from forty-nine (49) countries plus domestic scrap and metal trading firms, dealers and auction platforms, with import purchases rising from 23.05% of total purchases in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025; MoEFCC licensing requirements for lead scrap imports form a high entry barrier that the Company states it clears through low-emission technology investment and a record of regulatory compliance. Quality is controlled in-house via a testing laboratory aligning output with customer specifications. Forward linkage is through direct supply to lead-acid battery manufacturers and metal customers (the facility is deliberately sited near large battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility for short turnaround and lower logistics cost) and near Chennai (150 Kms), Kattupalli (130 Kms) and Ennore (130 Kms) ports for import of raw materials and export of finished products, supported by dedicated bulk storage areas for raw materials and finished products. Price risk across this chain is managed by a board-approved hedging framework: a back-to-back pricing model linking quoted prices to LME at order confirmation for both import and export transactions, and futures/derivative contracts exclusively on the LME, typically covering 60%-100% of exposure through forward contracts, with positions dynamically closed when buyers are confirmed. Planned further integration: converting internally generated plastic scrap/chips into plastic granules and refining/recycling tin and copper waste products on a 5.56-acre site at Menakur (V), Naidupet (M), Tirupati District provisionally allotted by APIIC. Sustainability inputs are integrated into the process — oxygen enrichment during manufacturing to reduce furnace-oil dependence, and green fuel derived from end-of-life tyres in place of coal and oil.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Mix shift from pure lead to higher-value lead alloys - lead alloys rose from 17.18% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2023 to 34.15% in Fiscal 2024 and 43.02% in Fiscal 2025, while pure lead fell from 70.51% to 42.34%
- Gross margin per ton expanded from INR 19,511.95 in Fiscal 2023 to INR 29,466.73 in Fiscal 2024 and INR 33,642.16 in Fiscal 2025, lifting EBITDA margin from 5.53% to 6.06% to 8.88%
- Export-led growth - export revenue CAGR of 521.22% from Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025, with export share of revenue from operations rising from 1.73% to 17.63% to 37.03%
- Raw material sourcing shift towards imported scrap - import operations rose from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025, contingent on timely MoEFCC licences and approvals
- Working capital intensity is the dominant funding need - INR 2,200.00 million of the INR 3,200.00 million Fresh Issue is for incremental working capital
- Rising leverage - total borrowings grew from INR 809.08 million in Fiscal 2023 to INR 1,423.60 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 1,657.66 million in Fiscal 2025 against net worth of INR 626.01 million in Fiscal 2025; INR 220.00 million of Net Proceeds is for repayment/pre-payment
- Cost levers from sustainability practices - oxygen incorporation during manufacturing reduces furnace oil dependence and green fuel from end-of-life tyres replaces coal and oil, enhancing productivity and optimising costs
- Capital efficiency improved - ROCE moved 19.77% (FY23) to 12.83% (FY24) to 25.17% (FY25) and RONW 42.38% to 30.61% to 53.15%, on a broadly steady fixed asset turnover of 10.44x, 10.22x and 11.15x
- Declining but still extreme customer concentration - top customer share fell from 85.73% (FY23) to 72.42% (FY24) to 51.22% (FY25); top 5 from 94.49% to 90.54% to 82.46%
- Lead price exposure managed through a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk and MCX benchmark pricing

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deepen participation in India's circular economy by closing the loop across collection, recycling and production, reducing dependence on imported critical metals and strengthening domestic resource security
- Complete the London Metal Exchange listing under 'Ardee Lead 9997' to establish international credibility and global price benchmarking, complementing the existing MCX listing
- Grow the export franchise from the Tirupati facility's port proximity, building on presence in seven countries as of March 31, 2025
- Shift mix further towards higher-value customisable lead alloys tailored to customer-specific purity and composition requirements
- Continue sustainability-led cost and efficiency initiatives - oxygen enrichment during manufacturing to cut furnace oil dependence and green fuel derived from end-of-life tyres in place of coal and oil
- Fund incremental working capital and reduce borrowings using Fresh Issue proceeds, and use the listing to enhance visibility and brand image among existing and potential customers

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Since the present Promoters acquired the Company in 2021, Ardee has invested continuously in its single owned Manufacturing Facility on approximately 7.61 acres at Naidupet, District Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, raising installed recycling capacity from 54,750 MTPA in Fiscal 2023 (unchanged in Fiscal 2024) to 104,025 MTPA in Fiscal 2025. Manufacturing capital expenditure was INR 252.98 million in Fiscal 2025, INR 205.36 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 220.29 million in Fiscal 2023, funding rotary furnaces, refining kettles, casting machines, pollution control systems and an in-house testing laboratory. The site was chosen for proximity to large lead-acid battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (short turnaround, lower logistics cost) and to Chennai, Kattupalli and Ennore ports for import of scrap and export of finished lead, with National Highway 16 / Golden Quadrilateral connectivity. Market expansion has run alongside capacity: exports reached seven countries and domestic sales ten states as of March 31, 2025. Notably, the Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for working capital and debt repayment rather than a new plant - no further capacity addition project is quantified in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of India's leading players in the circular economy for lead recycling with a proven track record and demonstrated operational stability (Source: F&S Report)
- Installed capacity nearly doubled from 54,750 MTPA in Fiscal 2023 to 104,025 MTPA in Fiscal 2025 following investment by the present promoters since their 2021 acquisition, backed by capex of INR 252.98 million, INR 205.36 million and INR 220.29 million in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023
- Regulatory entry barrier advantage - lead scrap imports require MoEFCC licensing and stringent compliance; a proven compliance record has kept approvals timely, lifting import operations from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025
- Strategic plant location in Tirupati close to large lead-acid battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, giving short turnaround times and lower logistics cost, and near Chennai (150 km), Kattupalli (130 km) and Ennore (130 km) ports for export/import
- Broad customisable product portfolio of pure lead plus five lead alloy families with purity from 99.97% to 99.985% conforming to international standards
- Brand 'Ardee' listed on MCX providing transparent benchmark pricing, hedging against price risk and market visibility; application filed for LME listing under 'Ardee Lead 9997'
- One of the fastest growing companies by revenue among its peers with a revenue CAGR of 33.15% over the last three Fiscals (Source: F&S Report)
- Strong customer base with robust raw material sourcing capability - 34, 29 and 14 repeat customers and 20, 25 and 28 new customers added in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023
- Track record of profitability and consistent financial performance; experienced promoters and professional management team
- Application of a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk protection

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Extreme customer concentration — The top customer contributed 51.22%, 72.42% and 85.73% of revenue from operations (INR 3,804.08 million, INR 3,352.94 million and INR 3,530.33 million) in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, and the top 5 customers 82.46%, 90.54% and 94.49%. Loss of any of these customers could materially affect business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
- Working capital intensity — INR 2,200.00 million of the INR 3,200.00 million Fresh Issue - the single largest object - is for incremental working capital, indicating a scrap-to-ingot cycle that consumes cash as revenue scales; the fund requirement is based on internal management estimates and has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- Leverage and refinancing dependence — Total borrowings rose from INR 809.08 million (FY23) to INR 1,423.60 million (FY24) to INR 1,657.66 million (FY25) versus net worth of only INR 626.01 million in FY25; only INR 220.00 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for repayment/pre-payment, so most debt remains outstanding post-Offer.
- Dependence on imported lead scrap and MoEFCC licensing — Lead scrap imports are subject to licensing and stringent MoEFCC compliance; import operations rose from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025, so any delay or denial of approvals would directly interrupt raw material supply and production.
- Single-location manufacturing — All 104,025 MTPA of installed capacity sits at one approximately 7.61-acre facility in Naidupet, District Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh; any disruption there (regulatory, environmental, utility or accident) halts the entire business.
- Lead commodity price volatility — Revenue and gross margin per ton are tied to lead prices; the Company relies on a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk protection and on MCX benchmark pricing, and a mismatch between scrap purchase cost and ingot realisation would compress the 8.88% EBITDA margin.
- Promoter concentration and recent change in control — Promoters hold 254,000,000 Equity Shares (99.68%) of the pre-Offer capital and are not the original promoters - control was acquired only under the share purchase agreement dated April 26, 2021, so the operating track record under current ownership is short.
- Reliance on a commissioned industry report — Industry and market claims - including the leading-player positioning and the 33.15% peer-relative revenue CAGR ranking - are derived from the F&S Report dated September 26, 2025, which was exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company, and reliance on it carries inherent risks.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Expand installed recycling capacity at the Tirupati Manufacturing Facility from 54,750 MTPA to 104,025 MTPA through continued investment since the Promoters' 2021 acquisition.**
- **Deploy INR 2,200.00 million of the Net Proceeds towards funding the incremental working capital requirement of the Company.**
- **Use INR 220.00 million of the Net Proceeds for repayment and/or pre-payment, in full or in part, of certain borrowings availed by the Company.**
- **Raise up to INR 3,200.00 million through the Fresh Issue of Equity Shares of face value INR 2 each, alongside an Offer for Sale of up to 37,650,000 Equity Shares by the Promoter Selling Shareholders.**
- **Cap the amount utilised for general corporate purposes at 25% of the Gross Proceeds in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations.**
- **Complete the pending application with the London Metal Exchange to list the Company's product under 'Ardee Lead 9997', to establish international credibility and global price benchmarking (the brand 'Ardee' is already listed on MCX).**
- **Grow international sales from the port-proximate Tirupati facility, building on exports to seven countries and a 37.03% export share of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025.**
- **Continue substituting fossil inputs in manufacturing - incorporating oxygen to reduce furnace oil dependence and using green fuel derived from end-of-life tyres in place of coal and oil - to enhance productivity and optimise costs.**
- **Maintain customisable product purity levels of 99.97% to 99.985% conforming to international standards, supported by an in-house testing laboratory and ISO 9001:2015 / 14001:2015 / 45001:2018 accreditations.**
- **Sustain the improving gross margin per ton, which rose from INR 19,511.95 in Fiscal 2023 to INR 29,466.73 in Fiscal 2024 and INR 33,642.16 in Fiscal 2025.**
- **Management flags dependence on its top customer and top 5 customers - 51.22% and 82.46% of Fiscal 2025 revenue from operations - and warns that losing any of them would materially hurt the business.**
- **Continued uninterrupted operations depend on timely MoEFCC licences for lead scrap imports, which have risen from 23.05% of import operations in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025.**
